title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
statement:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values (i.e., from left to right, level by level), as an array of arrays — one inner array per level.

Build a real `TreeNode` tree from `values`, then perform a standard BFS, processing one full level (queue snapshot) at a time.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 2000]

editorial.approach: Use a queue starting with the root (if it exists). At each iteration, capture the current queue's size (the number of nodes at this level), pop exactly that many nodes, collect their values into a level array, and push their children for the next round. Repeat until the queue is empty.
